title: Oriented nearby cycles, base-change comparison and Psi-good pairs
statement:
Let $f:T\to B$ be a morphism of schemes and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring. Use their small etale topoi [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with geometric morphisms in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Define the vanishing topos
$$V_f=T_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{B_{\mathrm{Et}}}B_{\mathrm{Et}}$$
to be the left oriented product of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] for $f:T_{\mathrm{Et}}\to B_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $\operatorname{id}:B_{\mathrm{Et}}\to B_{\mathrm{Et}}$, i.e. the topos of sheaves on the site of triples $(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ there, with $\mathcal C_1$ the small etale site of $T$, $\mathcal C_2=\mathcal D$ the small etale site of $B$, and the site inverse image $f^{-1}V=V\times_BT$: it has projections $p_1:V_f\to T_{\mathrm{Et}}$, $p_2:V_f\to B_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and a $2$-morphism $p_2\Rightarrow fp_1$, universal for this data by that lemma (equivalently, morphisms from any topos $\mathcal E$ to $V_f$ are pairs $a:\mathcal E\to T_{\mathrm{Et}}$, $b:\mathcal E\to B_{\mathrm{Et}}$ with a $2$-morphism $b\Rightarrow fa$). Here a $2$-morphism $u\Rightarrow w$ means a natural transformation $u_*\to w_*$, equivalently $w^{-1}\to u^{-1}$, as in [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. The morphism $\psi_f:T_{\mathrm{Et}}\to V_f$ corresponds to $(1_T,f,1_f)$. With constant coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] put
$$D(V_f,\Lambda)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{V_f})),\qquad R\Psi_f=R\psi_{f,*}.$$
The module and derived categories are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex] exist by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and total right derived direct image is their degreewise direct image as in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Derived tensor on any of these ringed topoi is the bifunctor of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], computed on K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex] using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For a geometric morphism $u$ between these constant-$\Lambda$ ringed topoi, write $u^*$ for its derived module inverse image: $u^{-1}\Lambda\cong\Lambda$, so it is the exact inverse image applied termwise. Use the module adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] and its derived adjunction $u^*\dashv Ru_*$ from [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors]; derived pullback exists and preserves derived tensor by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Thus $R\Psi_f:D(T_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)\to D(V_f,\Lambda)$ is defined on the unbounded derived categories, extending the usual bounded-below convention. $D^b$ means cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval.

For $f':T'\to B'$, a commutative square with $h:T'\to T$, $g:B'\to B$ and $fh=gf'$ induces $v:V_{f'}\to V_f$: apply [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] to the projections $hp'_1$, $gp'_2$ and the $2$-morphism $gp'_2\Rightarrow gf'p'_1=fhp'_1$. It gives $v\psi_{f'}\cong\psi_fh$ with their projection identifications. For $L\in D(T_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ define the ordinary comparison $\beta_{h,g,L}:v^*R\Psi_fL\to R\Psi_{f'}h^*L$ as the transpose under $\psi_{f'}^*\dashv R\Psi_{f'}$ of the composite
$$\psi_{f'}^*v^*R\Psi_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}h^*\psi_f^*R\Psi_fL\xrightarrow{h^*\varepsilon_{f,L}}h^*L,$$
where $\varepsilon_f$ is the counit of $\psi_f^*\dashv R\Psi_f$. The pair $(f,L)$ is called $\Psi$-good if this map is an isomorphism for every Cartesian square obtained by an arbitrary scheme morphism $g:B'\to B$. For $L,M\in D(T_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ the lax tensor map $\mu_{f,L,M}:R\Psi_fL\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Psi_fM\to R\Psi_f(L\otimes^L_\Lambda M)$ is the transpose under that same adjunction of
$$\psi_f^*(R\Psi_fL\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Psi_fM)\xrightarrow{\sim}\psi_f^*R\Psi_fL\otimes^L_\Lambda\psi_f^*R\Psi_fM\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{f,L}\otimes^L\varepsilon_{f,M}}L\otimes^L_\Lambda M.$$

For two morphisms $f_i:T_i\to B$, put $T=T_1\times_BT_2$, let $f:T\to B$ be the structure map, let $q_i:T\to T_i$ be the projections and $v_i:V_f\to V_{f_i}$ the induced maps. For $L_i\in D(T_{i,\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ and $P_i\in D(V_{f_i},\Lambda)$, on $T$ write $L_1\boxtimes_B^LL_2=q_1^*L_1\otimes_\Lambda^Lq_2^*L_2$; on $V_f$ write $P_1\boxtimes^LP_2=v_1^*P_1\otimes_\Lambda^Lv_2^*P_2$. Define the oriented Kunneth comparison by
$$v_1^*R\Psi_{f_1}L_1\otimes^L_\Lambda v_2^*R\Psi_{f_2}L_2\xrightarrow{\beta_{q_1,1_B,L_1}\otimes^L\beta_{q_2,1_B,L_2}}R\Psi_f(q_1^*L_1)\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Psi_f(q_2^*L_2)\xrightarrow{\mu_{f,q_1^*L_1,q_2^*L_2}}R\Psi_f(L_1\boxtimes_B^LL_2).$$

split_report.summary: Second reading repaired missing statement dependencies for constant sheaves, unbounded K-injective derivation, derived tensor, module adjunction and derived tensor-preserving pullback. Made the site/topos distinction, 2-morphism convention, domains, ordinary comparison transpose, lax tensor transpose and Kunneth composite explicit. Independently read Illusie 1.4--1.5 and 2.1; no new nodes, no changed mathematical scope, and no invertibility or finiteness assertion added.
split_report.blueprint: The item realizes the auxiliary oriented construction and vanishing-topos definitions used in the trace-formula route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q19-b5e90608b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full, all 15 statement dependencies, the four DAG users and the base statement. I also read ILO Exposé XI 1.1–1.7, 1.9 and 4.1–4.4 in the local PDF. The vanishing topos meets every hypothesis of lem-trf-oriented-product-universal: étale sites with finite limits under pretopologies, and the base-change functor V×_B T is continuous and preserves finite limits. The covering (c) and the 2-morphism p₂ ⇒ f p₁ match ILO 1.1 and 4.3, and ψ_f=(1_T,f,1_f) matches ILO 4.3(4.b). The map v comes from (h p′₁, g p′₂, gτ′) as in ILO 1.9, and vψ_{f′}≅ψ_f h follows from uniqueness in the universal property. β is the correct base-change mate: for an identity square it is the identity by the triangle identity. μ is the transpose of ε⊗ε, and the Künneth composite β⊗β followed by μ has endpoints matching lem-trf-good-oriented-nearby-kunneth. The derived machinery is supplied by the added dependencies: K-injective existence, the right derived functor, derived tensor descent, the module and derived adjunctions, and tensor-preserving pullback. Their hypotheses hold, and u⁻¹Λ≅Λ is elementary. Compared with the base statement there is no weakening and no added hypothesis; Ψ-goodness still requires every base change g. Small cases checked: punctual B, T=∅, Λ=0, f=id and the identity square. There are no new nodes, no duplicates (rg search of the DAG), no cycle (traversal), no SGA source and no tool_uses. Illusie's Thom–Sebastiani paper is not available locally and I could not fetch it, so I did not read it; the node still correctly marks it WANTED, although the report claims the source reference was updated. One recorded grep verdict has cosmetic text copied from another search. No fixes were made.
